rituals.title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
rituals.ritual_name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
rituals.goal: Make an intentionally imperfect start, repair one useful part, and stop polishing — rejoin broken link.
rituals.steps:
1. Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, rough mental outline, or unfinished opening.
3. Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

rituals.win: The rough beginning became editable after exactly one correction instead of needing to become impressive.

rituals.name: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
rituals.title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
rituals.goal: Patch open gap; test whether a thought actually clarifies, protects, and leaves you more capable.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move.
2. Does it protect something real.
3. Does it leave me more capable afterward.
4. Score each yes or no.
5. If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
rituals.winReward: A thought that failed most of the test lost its advisory role without needing to be argued out of existence.
rituals.win: A thought that failed most of the test lost its advisory role without needing to be argued out of existence.
rituals.mindBend: Not every protective-sounding thought is useful counsel. Advice earns authority by what it helps you do afterward.
rituals.formulaFlow: Ask Thought → Check Protection → Leave Me → Score Yes → Thank Warning

display.goal: Patch open gap; test whether a thought actually clarifies, protects, and leaves you more capable.
display.numberedSteps:

rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE THE FEED BEFORE CRAVING VOTES

rituals.name: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
rituals.title: THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE
rituals.goal: Move one swinging habit into a middle range you could repeat for two weeks — set current rhythm.
rituals.steps:
1. Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.
rituals.winReward: Sleep, food, effort, practice, or rest shifted toward a sustainable band instead of another extreme.
rituals.win: Sleep, food, effort, practice, or rest shifted toward a sustainable band instead of another extreme.
rituals.mindBend: Extremes can feel committed because they are intense. Repeatability is a better test of whether a routine can actually carry you.
rituals.formulaFlow: Rest Review → Find Area → Set Middle → Choose Smallest

rituals.name: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
rituals.title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
rituals.goal: Separate the raw facts of an event from the connections your mind constructed around them; test crossed signal.
rituals.steps:
1. Take one rigid reading of an event.
2. Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
4. Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.
rituals.winReward: One alternate interpretation changed lived experience without requiring the original facts to change.
rituals.win: One alternate interpretation changed lived experience without requiring the original facts to change.
rituals.mindBend: A convincing interpretation can be assembled from fragments just like a dream. Coherence is not the same as proof.
rituals.formulaFlow: Take Event → Compare Dream → Identify Facts → Try Construction
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid dreamlike framing if it increases feelings of unreality, unusual perceptions, or loss of contact with what is real.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
rituals.title: FIND WHERE THE PATTERN MISSED
rituals.goal: Ease heavy load: find the conditions under which a recurring pattern is weaker, then recreate one.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.
rituals.winReward: Two exceptions revealed one influenceable condition that could be deliberately placed into the next similar situation.
rituals.win: Two exceptions revealed one influenceable condition that could be deliberately placed into the next similar situation.
rituals.mindBend: A pattern's exceptions are not noise. They are clues to the conditions that keep the pattern from becoming inevitable.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Pattern → Find Misses → Compare Conditions → Transplant Edge
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Exceptions do not make unsafe situations safe; do not use this game to blame yourself for trauma, illness, abuse, discrimination, or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

display.goal: Ease heavy load: find the conditions under which a recurring pattern is weaker, then recreate one.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.
display.win: Two exceptions revealed one influenceable condition that could be deliberately placed into the next similar situation.
display.mindBend: A pattern's exceptions are not noise. They are clues to the conditions that keep the pattern from becoming inevitable.
display.formulaFlow: Name Pattern → Find Misses → Compare Conditions → Transplant Edge

safety.raw:
PAUSE
Exceptions do not make unsafe situations safe; do not use this game to blame yourself for trauma, illness, abuse, discrimination, or coercion.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
rituals.title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
rituals.goal: Stop refreshing one mental construction and let the existing residue fade by itself — repair needed boundary.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.
2. For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.winReward: No new scene, argument, or confirmation was added while attention moved into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.win: No new scene, argument, or confirmation was added while attention moved into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.mindBend: Some mental content persists because it is being repeatedly republished — ending the renewal is different from forcing the old copy away.
rituals.formulaFlow: Identify Image → Time → Let Existing → Redirect

rituals.name: THE EXTRA MEANING CHECK
rituals.title: THE EXTRA MEANING CHECK
rituals.goal: Filter loud distortion; separate the facts about someone else from fears or old rules you may be adding.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the quality you think you see in the other person.
2. Ask what fear, expectation, or old rule in you makes that quality stand out.
3. Name the external evidence separately.
4. Keep what the facts support and question the extra meaning.
rituals.winReward: The external facts kept their weight while unsupported extra meaning became something you could question.
rituals.win: The external facts kept their weight while unsupported extra meaning became something you could question.
rituals.mindBend: Something may truly have happened while your mind also adds meaning from older fears or rules. Both can be checked separately.
rituals.formulaFlow: Picture Quality → Ask Internal → Name External → Keep Facts

rituals.name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.ritual_name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.goal: Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another; find deeper stillness.
rituals.steps:
1. Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count the gap only after it is over.
rituals.winReward: A real gap appeared before the next thought arrived on its own, even if it lasted only a fraction.
rituals.win: A real gap appeared before the next thought arrived on its own, even if it lasted only a fraction.
rituals.mindBend: The mind can hide silence by commenting on it. The first post-gap thought can make the gap seem absent.
rituals.formulaFlow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap

PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: EFFORT IS STILL AVAILABLE
rituals.title: EFFORT IS STILL AVAILABLE
rituals.goal: Unload excess load: put effort into the smallest part of the situation that is still changeable.
rituals.steps:
1. Name what cannot be changed today.
2. Beside it, name the smallest domain where effort remains possible.
3. Take one concrete step there before returning to contemplation.
4. Let action answer the part of the problem that is actually yours.
rituals.winReward: One concrete action happened in the domain you could influence instead of circling what could not move.
rituals.win: One concrete action happened in the domain you could influence instead of circling what could not move.
rituals.mindBend: Powerlessness grows when changeable and unchangeable parts are mentally mixed. Separating them returns effort to a real target.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Cannot → Name Smallest → Take Concrete → Let Action

rituals.name: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
rituals.title: RUN THE START GATE TWICE
rituals.goal: Rehearse the opening movements twice, then enter the real task through the same doorway — drop unneeded weight.
rituals.steps:
1. Mentally rehearse the first few movements that would begin the task.
2. Run that opening sequence once in imagination without producing work.
3. Return the imagined scene to neutral once.
4. Repeat the same sequence, then begin the real task from its first movement.
rituals.winReward: The imagined start became the actual first movement without needing a new round of planning.
rituals.win: The imagined start became the actual first movement without needing a new round of planning.
rituals.mindBend: Starting can become easier when the body has already run the first seconds. Rehearsal reduces the novelty at the threshold.
rituals.formulaFlow: Stage Door → Dry Launch → Reset → Live Entry

PAUSE

rituals.name: DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD
rituals.title: DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD
rituals.goal: Lighten emotional load; hold two opposite experiences clearly while noticing the space that contains both.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
2. Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Then include the shared field in which both are present.
4. Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.
rituals.winReward: Difference stayed vivid without forcing either side to erase the other or become total separation.
rituals.win: Difference stayed vivid without forcing either side to erase the other or become total separation.
rituals.mindBend: Opposites can share one field without becoming the same — distinction does not require disconnection.
rituals.formulaFlow: Contrasting → Hold Distinct → Include Shared → Let Difference
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use ordinary distinctions when boundaries or safety require clear separation.

rituals.goal: Do the required behaviour precisely while postponing the inner argument about it; mend open gap.
rituals.steps:
1. Set the exact external behaviour required.

rituals.name: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
rituals.title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
rituals.goal: Steady anchored attention: make another thinking lap pay for the time it takes from real life.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.
rituals.winReward: The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.
rituals.win: The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.
rituals.mindBend: Mental time feels free because its cost is invisible — naming what it replaces turns rumination into a real transaction.

rituals.name: THE EMOTION LINEUP
rituals.title: THE EMOTION LINEUP
rituals.goal: Mend repairable break; check whether the first emotion you named is the one your body is actually signalling.
rituals.steps:

2. Check the body clues: heat, heaviness, tightness, energy, urge, and location.

rituals.name: ROTATE THE CHAIR
rituals.title: ROTATE THE CHAIR
rituals.goal: View the same event from your view, the other person’s possible view, a neutral view, and future-you — reduce emotional burden.
rituals.steps:
1. Describe the event from your position.
2. Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
3. Stand as a neutral observer and keep only observable behaviour.
4. Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.

rituals.win: Facts and guesses became easier to separate after the event was seen from four different positions.

rituals.name: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
rituals.title: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
rituals.goal: Balance current priorities; turn one claim about another person’s motive into three possibilities and one question.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.

rituals.title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
rituals.ritual_name: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
rituals.goal: Say the unsent truth in your mind, then leave contact alone for a full day — rejoin missing thread.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine the person in front of you.
2. In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

rituals.title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON

rituals.name: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
rituals.title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
rituals.goal: Ground quiet pace; put past actions, present repairs, and future prevention back into their correct time zones.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
4. Do only one PRESENT task now.
rituals.winReward: Misplaced tasks moved to the right period, leaving one genuinely present action to do now.
rituals.win: Misplaced tasks moved to the right period, leaving one genuinely present action to do now.
rituals.mindBend: Guilt and worry often mix time zones. A past event cannot be repaired by a future plan that never becomes a present action.

rituals.name: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
rituals.title: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
rituals.goal: Turn one looming deadline into separate usable work blocks with visible finishes; contain raw charge.
rituals.steps:
1. Count the usable work blocks remaining, subtracting sleep and fixed duties.
2. Give each block one deliverable with a visible finish.
3. Place buffers before the final deadline.
4. Start the earliest window; refuse to mentally carry later windows inside it.
rituals.winReward: Sleep and fixed duties were respected, buffers existed, and only the earliest work window was mentally active.
rituals.win: Sleep and fixed duties were respected, buffers existed, and only the earliest work window was mentally active.
rituals.mindBend: A deadline feels monolithic when every future block is carried at once; dividing time restores sequence and reduces false immediacy.

1. Each time the same future scene repeats, extract one actionable item: question, document, rehearsal, route, support, or if-then link.
2. Add it to a checklist.
3. When repetition yields no new preparation, stamp the simulation PAID IN FULL and switch to execution.
display.win: Each useful repetition became a checklist item, and the loop closed once no new preparation emerged.
display.mindBend: Anticipation earns its keep only while it changes readiness. After that, the simulation is charging attention for already-paid information.
display.formulaFlow: Repeat Extract → Add Checklist → Stamp Simulation

rituals.name: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
rituals.title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
rituals.goal: Give the body’s aftershock time to settle before letting it change what the event meant — expose background interference.
rituals.steps:
1. Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, mental loops, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes.
2. Picture its end time.
3. Until then, keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened.
4. Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible.
rituals.winReward: Shakiness, fatigue, or looping were treated as echoes until the chosen reassessment point rather than fresh evidence.
rituals.win: Shakiness, fatigue, or looping were treated as echoes until the chosen reassessment point rather than fresh evidence.

rituals.name: BODY SIGNAL, STORY LATER
rituals.title: BODY SIGNAL, STORY LATER
rituals.goal: Patch missing piece; notice one ordinary part of your life as if you had just regained access to it.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine briefly that you lost access to your current life and then unexpectedly got it back.
2. Notice what small thing would suddenly matter: someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, or morning light.
3. Do one thing today that honours that value without pretending real hardship is okay.
rituals.winReward: One ordinary part of life felt more valuable, and one action honoured it without denying real hardship.

rituals.name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.goal: Restore the real time distance between events that currently feel piled together; hold brief pause.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
rituals.winReward: Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.
rituals.win: Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.
rituals.mindBend: The mind can compress years into one emotional cluster. Spacing time visually reduces the false message that everything is happening now.

rituals.name: A NOTE FROM TOMORROW MORNING
rituals.title: A NOTE FROM TOMORROW MORNING
rituals.goal: Stitch loose thread: let tomorrow-you protect one thing that tonight's urge may forget.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture tomorrow-you after tonight’s urge has passed. Ask what one thing they want protected: sleep, money, sobriety, dignity, preparation, or safety.
2. Mentally sign the request with tomorrow’s date.
3. Bring that promise to mind exactly where the immediate choice happens.
rituals.winReward: A dated promise about sleep, money, sobriety, dignity, preparation, or safety reached the exact choice point.

rituals.name: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
rituals.title: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
rituals.goal: Describe the body's physics before choosing an emotion label or story — redirect rising surge.
rituals.steps:
1. For twenty seconds, ban emotion names and causes.
2. Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
3. At the bell, choose the smallest plain word that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.
rituals.winReward: Shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, and pulse were noticed before a simple feeling word was allowed in.
rituals.win: Shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, and pulse were noticed before a simple feeling word was allowed in.
rituals.mindBend: Emotion words can pull a story in behind them. Raw sensation sometimes reveals that the body data was narrower than the label.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Causes → Describe Geometry → Choose Smallest

rituals.name: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
rituals.title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
rituals.goal: Quiet steady moment; turn identity verdicts into temporary processes that can change under conditions.
rituals.steps:
1. Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
3. Add one condition under which the process changes.
rituals.winReward: 'I am' became a description of what is happening, when it increased, and when it shifts.
rituals.win: 'I am' became a description of what is happening, when it increased, and when it shifts.
rituals.mindBend: A noun-like identity feels permanent. Process language exposes movement, timing, and conditions that a label hides.
rituals.formulaFlow: Drop Verb → Use Temporary → Add Condition

display.title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
display.goal: Quiet steady moment; turn identity verdicts into temporary processes that can change under conditions.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
3. Add one condition under which the process changes.
display.win: 'I am' became a description of what is happening, when it increased, and when it shifts.
display.mindBend: A noun-like identity feels permanent. Process language exposes movement, timing, and conditions that a label hides.
display.formulaFlow: Drop Verb → Use Temporary → Add Condition

rituals.title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
rituals.goal: Step back from the mind's content without stepping away from the action you own; settle steady quiet.
rituals.steps:

2. Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance the content, not agency.

rituals.win: The prediction was described at a distance, then first-person agency returned exactly where behaviour began.

rituals.name: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
rituals.title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
rituals.ritual_name: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
rituals.goal: Read useful signal: let a troubling image reach its own final frame without adding verbal commentary.
rituals.steps:
1. Bring up the image gently and prohibit verbal commentary.
2. Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
3. Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes.
4. Reorient afterward using present sensory facts.
rituals.winReward: The image moved to a stable ending and your present sensory surroundings were restored afterward.
rituals.win: The image moved to a stable ending and your present sensory surroundings were restored afterward.
rituals.mindBend: An image can remain unfinished because commentary repeatedly interrupts its motion. Allowing the visual sequence to complete may reveal a different endpoint.
rituals.formulaFlow: Bring Image → Allow Move → Check Position → Use Sensory

rituals.name: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
rituals.title: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
rituals.goal: Spend one minute with direct sensation before concepts are allowed to explain it — channel extra energy.
rituals.steps:
1. Set a brief interval.
2. During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
3. Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
4. If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.
rituals.winReward: Colour, sound, contact, and movement continued while labels, comparisons, and solutions were treated as later additions.
rituals.win: Colour, sound, contact, and movement continued while labels, comparisons, and solutions were treated as later additions.
rituals.mindBend: Explanation can arrive so fast that direct experience becomes background; removing concepts briefly shows what was there before the commentary.
rituals.formulaFlow: Set Brief → Name Comparisons → Attend Direct → Let Sensory

rituals.name: MUTE THE INNER SUBTITLES
rituals.title: MUTE THE INNER SUBTITLES
rituals.goal: Do one ordinary activity without narrating it from inside your head; harness extra energy.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose washing, walking, eating, or dressing.
2. For the duration, omit internal narration and meet only sensation and movement.
3. When commentary resumes, do not answer it; rejoin the activity at the next contact point.

rituals.win: Commentary returned, went unanswered, and attention rejoined the next real contact point of the activity.

rituals.name: MEANING ON HOLD
rituals.title: MEANING ON HOLD
rituals.goal: Release borrowed weight: delay meaning until facts from several channels are actually present.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the event without explaining it.
2. Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
3. Until all three exist, name every meaning temporary.
4. Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.
rituals.winReward: Observed facts and timing came first; the final meaning stayed no broader than the evidence.
rituals.win: Observed facts and timing came first; the final meaning stayed no broader than the evidence.
rituals.mindBend: Meaning rushes to fill missing information — making it temporary prevents the first explanation from becoming the permanent one.
rituals.formulaFlow: Hold Event → Find Facts → Name Meaning → Assign Narrowest

rituals.name: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
rituals.title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
rituals.ritual_name: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
rituals.goal: Replace inflammatory language with the exact frequency, loss, or behaviour it refers to — reinforce missing link.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
rituals.title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
rituals.goal: Preserve the original prediction when reality surprises it; trace mental noise.
rituals.steps:
1. The moment an outcome differs from expectation, keep both versions verbatim.
2. State the size and direction of the error.
3. Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Do not let hindsight rewrite the original prediction.
rituals.winReward: The expected outcome and the actual outcome stayed side by side, forcing the old model to account for its miss.
rituals.win: The expected outcome and the actual outcome stayed side by side, forcing the old model to account for its miss.

rituals.name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.goal: Unhook mental loop: make fear state exactly what should happen, by when, and how confident it is.
rituals.steps:
1. Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Use the result to update confidence in either direction.

rituals.name: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
rituals.title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
rituals.goal: Keep felt certainty on a different meter from the quality of the evidence — trace loud distortion.
rituals.steps:
1. Rate how sure you feel from 0–100.
2. Independently rate evidence quality using source reliability, directness, and recency.
3. Picture the two scores on separate meters so certainty cannot masquerade as evidence.
4. Let the evidence meter choose the action; treat the confidence meter as a feeling to notice, not a vote.
rituals.winReward: The action followed source reliability, directness, and recency rather than the number measuring how sure you felt.
rituals.win: The action followed source reliability, directness, and recency rather than the number measuring how sure you felt.
rituals.mindBend: Confidence is an internal sensation — evidence is information about the world, and the two can move independently.
rituals.formulaFlow: Rate Sure → Rate Evidence → Separate Meters → Follow Evidence

rituals.name: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER

rituals.goal: Look once for the sign that should be present if the feared model is right; reconnect missing piece.
rituals.steps:

3. If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

display.goal: Keep the threat in view while widening attention to what is happening around it — expose subtle distortion.

rituals.name: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
rituals.title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
rituals.goal: Settle steady stillness; practise moving attention between tiny detail and the whole scene.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture one simple shape.
2. Spend ten slow counts on one tiny feature.
3. Spend ten counts on the whole shape and the space around it.
4. Move back to detail, then choose the view that best fits your task.
rituals.winReward: You could zoom in, zoom out, and deliberately choose the view that fit the task.
rituals.win: You could zoom in, zoom out, and deliberately choose the view that fit the task.
rituals.mindBend: Attention has a focal length. Being stuck at one zoom can distort importance even when the information itself is accurate.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Shape → Zoom Detail → Widen View → Reverse

rituals.name: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
rituals.title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
rituals.goal: Separate how noticeable information feels from how much it actually changes the decision; mend shared connection.
rituals.steps:
1. Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
2. A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the priority list.
3. Allocate attention to decision impact instead.
rituals.winReward: A vivid low-impact item lost priority while attention moved toward what mattered for the choice.
rituals.win: A vivid low-impact item lost priority while attention moved toward what mattered for the choice.
rituals.mindBend: What grabs attention is not always what matters. Dramatic information can feel important without earning much influence on the decision.
rituals.formulaFlow: Score Information → Pay Felt → Allocate Attention

rituals.title: GROUNDING ANCHOR RELAY
rituals.goal: Interrupt repeating cycle: rotate through several grounding channels and keep the one that restores the clearest present contact.

2. Spend a short interval with each and switch before getting used to it empties it.
3. Finish on the channel that restored the clearest present contact.

rituals.win: Visual, auditory, pressure, and joint cues were tested before one channel became the final anchor.

rituals.name: BRAID THE SIGNALS
rituals.title: BRAID THE SIGNALS
rituals.goal: Let two competing signals share attention before deciding which one matters — check working sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose the two signals fighting for attention.
2. Alternate A–B–A–B at a slow fixed rhythm.
3. Then hold both at the same time for one interval, noticing difference without choosing.
4. Decide only after the braid is complete.
rituals.winReward: A–B alternation became simultaneous awareness, and the decision waited until both signals had been fully represented.
rituals.win: A–B alternation became simultaneous awareness, and the decision waited until both signals had been fully represented.
rituals.mindBend: Attention can falsely create a winner by showing one signal at a time; holding both changes the comparison.
rituals.formulaFlow: Choose Signals → Alternate B → Hold Time → Decide After

rituals.title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
rituals.ritual_name: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
rituals.goal: Mend working gap; give a truly finished topic one repeatable sensory ending and a clear return time.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
2. Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
3. Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.

rituals.ritual_name: MOVE NOVELTY TO THE RIGHT TEAM
rituals.goal: Move novelty into the useful task instead of letting novelty pull you away from it; test hidden distortion.

2. Mentally add variety to the desired task by changing order, challenge, or approach.

rituals.name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.ritual_name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.goal: Balance real choices: match two sides of physical pressure, then lower both together back to zero.
rituals.steps:
1. Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.
rituals.winReward: Equal resistance stepped down through lighter levels until your hands rested and the urge to press could be checked.
rituals.win: Equal resistance stepped down through lighter levels until your hands rested and the urge to press could be checked.
rituals.mindBend: The body can learn release through symmetry. Lowering matched pressure together shows that stopping does not require one side to lose.
rituals.formulaFlow: Press Equal → Match Force → Step Down → Reach Zero

rituals.name: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.goal: Interrupt stuck pattern; change only the quietest safe channel of body alarm and leave the louder ones alone.
rituals.steps:
1. Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.
rituals.winReward: Speed, pressure, and temperature were read separately, then one lower-intensity channel moved a single step.
rituals.win: Speed, pressure, and temperature were read separately, then one lower-intensity channel moved a single step.
rituals.mindBend: The loudest symptom is not always the best doorway — working with the easiest channel can change the system without fighting its strongest signal.
rituals.formulaFlow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel

rituals.name: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
rituals.title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
rituals.ritual_name: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
rituals.goal: Separate true signal: choose an action that crosses none of your emotions' reasonable red lines.
rituals.steps:
1. Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Observe them before deciding.
2. Give each emotion one safe veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Mentally remove actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty.
4. Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.
rituals.winReward: Several feelings named one safe veto each, leaving a move that no emotion loved but none had to betray.
rituals.win: Several feelings named one safe veto each, leaving a move that no emotion loved but none had to betray.
rituals.mindBend: Compromise inside yourself is not averaging emotions; it can mean finding a move that respects every valid boundary at once.
rituals.formulaFlow: Seat Feelings → Vetoes → Clear Board → Choose Survivor

PAUSE

rituals.win: The verdict became temporary and specific enough to reveal one condition that could actually change.

display.title: PRACTISE THE QUALITY ANONYMOUSLY
display.goal: Strip rising static; try one unfamiliar positive quality privately before deciding whether it belongs to you.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Choose a positive quality that feels ‘not me’. Do one behaviour that shows it without announcing a new identity.
2. Ask the brave question, make the playful move, accept the compliment, or set the clear boundary.
3. Let the behaviour become evidence before deciding what it says about you.
display.win: The behaviour happened before you had to approve a new identity.
display.mindBend: Identity often follows behaviour. A quality can start feeling believable after you practise it, not before.
display.formulaFlow: Choose Positive → Ask Brave → Await Proof

rituals.name: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
rituals.title: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
rituals.goal: Remove the imagined audience and choose from direct consequences plus values; shape useful energy.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action.
2. Erase the imagined audience one row at a time.
3. What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained.
4. Take the smallest version privately.
rituals.winReward: Praise, criticism, reposts, and reputation disappeared from the decision, leaving one private action you still wanted.
rituals.win: Praise, criticism, reposts, and reputation disappeared from the decision, leaving one private action you still wanted.
rituals.mindBend: Audience pressure can hide inside preference. Removing every witness reveals which part of the desire survives without social payment.

rituals.name: BLANK THE NAMEPLATE
rituals.title: BLANK THE NAMEPLATE
rituals.goal: Cut mental loop: make one decision without consulting the identity label you usually use to predict yourself.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the identity label on a removable card and turn it face down.
2. For the next decision, refer only to capacities, needs, facts, and values.
3. Choose.
4. Then uncover the label and compare what it would have predicted.

rituals.name: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.goal: Let different inner needs speak once, then give coordination to the part protecting the whole system — quiet extra noise.
rituals.steps:
1. Give each self-state an imagined place.
2. One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Appoint an inner coordinator whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Let that coordinator combine, delay, or reject proposals while acknowledging every need.
rituals.winReward: Each self-state was heard without becoming the chairperson, and one coordinator decided what could combine, wait, or be declined.
rituals.win: Each self-state was heard without becoming the chairperson, and one coordinator decided what could combine, wait, or be declined.
rituals.mindBend: Inner conflict becomes chaos when every need behaves like an emergency executive. Acknowledgement does not require equal authority.
rituals.formulaFlow: Give Self → Sentence → Protect Whole → Guide Council

PAUSE
Use professional support if parts feel autonomous, dangerous, or disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
rituals.title: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
rituals.ritual_name: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
rituals.goal: Cut tight spiral; spend one minute in direct experience without using your biography to explain who is here.
rituals.steps:
1. For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
2. Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
4. Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.
rituals.winReward: Sound, pressure, light, and movement continued while name, status, history, and plans stayed temporarily offline.
rituals.win: Sound, pressure, light, and movement continued while name, status, history, and plans stayed temporarily offline.
rituals.mindBend: Your biography is a powerful model of you, but experience keeps occurring even during the brief moments when the model is not being consulted.
rituals.formulaFlow: Don't Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if life-story quiet creates feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: WIDEN THE PRESENT CAMERA
rituals.title: WIDEN THE PRESENT CAMERA
rituals.goal: Widen your view of the current room when a memory feels too close; steady high charge.
rituals.steps:
1. Rest your eyes on a plain object and name its colour.
2. Shift to a second object farther away and name its shape.
3. Turn your head slowly and identify the room’s widest visible edge.
4. Say your current location and choose the next ordinary action.
rituals.winReward: Attention moved from one close cue to the wider room and a present-day action.
rituals.win: Attention moved from one close cue to the wider room and a present-day action.
rituals.mindBend: When attention narrows, a memory can fill the frame. Widening the real visual field gives the present more space.
rituals.formulaFlow: Fix Object → Shift Farther → Widen Room → Choose Action
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and use only the room that is actually around you. Do not picture, revisit, or change the memory. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less oriented, and connect with qualified human support.
This is present-day grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: THEN, NOW, NEXT
rituals.title: THEN, NOW, NEXT
rituals.goal: Mend small bridge: restore time order without retelling the painful event.
rituals.steps:
1. Name only the year or life stage when the event happened; add no details.
2. Read today’s date aloud, then name the place you are in.
3. Name one real thing in your life now that did not exist then.
4. Name the next ordinary thing you will do within ten minutes.
rituals.winReward: Then, now, and next became separate time points without reopening the event.
rituals.win: Then, now, and next became separate time points without reopening the event.
rituals.mindBend: Trauma alarm can flatten time. A simple timeline restores sequence without asking the memory to tell its story again.
rituals.formulaFlow: Mark Then → Name Now → Spot Difference → Name Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only a date or life stage for the past; do not add sensory detail, imagery, or a retelling. Stop if you feel unreal, disconnected, overwhelmed, or less oriented, and connect with qualified human support.
This is present-day grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
rituals.title: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
rituals.ritual_name: SAVE THE LESSON, DELETE THE VERDICT
rituals.goal: Soften pressure: keep the specific lesson from a painful event without letting it become a verdict on your whole life.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the specific lesson the event genuinely supports.
2. Notice the global conclusion attached to it: ‘Nobody is safe,’ ‘I am weak,’ ‘Life is over,’ or another all-life verdict.
3. Ask whether the specific lesson still works without the global verdict. Keep what teaches; delete what condemns.
rituals.winReward: A useful lesson survived after the global condemnation was removed.
rituals.win: A useful lesson survived after the global condemnation was removed.
rituals.mindBend: Experience can teach caution without proving 'always', 'nobody', or 'I am'; wisdom becomes distorted when one event is promoted into a law.

rituals.name: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
rituals.goal: Let a random workable section choose the starting point when order does not matter — patch working connection.
rituals.steps:
1. Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let the first number that pops into your mind choose the section. Do not pick again just because you dislike it.
3. Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.

45–60 seconds

GOAL
Rebuild working bridge: leave the future version of you one exact phrase that points back into the task.

STEPS
1. Before stopping, picture the exact next movement and current reasoning.
2. Hold one short phrase that tells you where to resume.
3. End the task without mentally reopening the whole plan.
4. On return, use the phrase and continue from that exact point.

WIN
The task ended with the next movement and reasoning preserved, so return did not require reopening the whole plan.

MIND BEND
Stopping is less costly when context is intentionally cached. A bridge back prevents tomorrow from paying today's setup cost again.

FORMULA FLOW
Stop Precise → Mark Re-entry → Leave Cleanly → Return

SAFETY
PAUSE
Update the bridge when conditions or priorities change.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS
rituals.title: THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS
rituals.goal: Finish the smallest version that still serves the task's essential purpose; unhook loud echo.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the task’s essential purpose.
2. Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
3. Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.
rituals.winReward: Nonessential features were removed and a usable deliverable existed before any optional upgrade.
rituals.win: Nonessential features were removed and a usable deliverable existed before any optional upgrade.
rituals.mindBend: Perfectionism treats every feature as structural. Defining the purpose reveals which parts are decoration.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Task → Remove Feature → Build Smallest

2. Store the script beside the behaviour.

rituals.name: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD
rituals.title: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD
rituals.ritual_name: COME BACK FROM THEIR IMAGINED HEAD
rituals.goal: Sort claims about another person's mind into known, inferred, and unknowable — lighten old weight.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture three boxes: KNOWN, INFERRED, UNKNOWABLE.
2. Move every claim about the other person into its correct box.
3. Choose one direct question or boundary based on known facts.
4. Leave the unknowable box empty of action.
rituals.winReward: Your next question or boundary used known facts while the unknowable box stayed empty of action.
rituals.win: Your next question or boundary used known facts while the unknowable box stayed empty of action.
rituals.mindBend: Imagined motives feel actionable because they arrive as sentences — putting them in an unknowable box prevents guesses from becoming instructions.
rituals.formulaFlow: Sort Boxes → Move Claim → Choose Direct → Leave Unknowable

rituals.name: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
rituals.title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
rituals.ritual_name: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
rituals.goal: Loosen familiar cycle; reduce exactly one kind of access without shutting down the entire relationship.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.
rituals.winReward: Time, topic, channel, location, or frequency changed by one level while the other doors remained untouched.
rituals.win: Time, topic, channel, location, or frequency changed by one level while the other doors remained untouched.
rituals.mindBend: Contact is not a single switch. Adjusting one door can create safety without forcing the whole relationship into open-or-closed thinking.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Contact → Pick Door → Lower One → Hold Setting

rituals.name: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
rituals.title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
rituals.goal: Understand the other view accurately, then place your disagreement in its own sentence; aim hot impulse.
rituals.steps:
1. Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
2. Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
4. No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.
rituals.winReward: Their position was recognisable before your different meaning, value, or decision was stated.
rituals.win: Their position was recognisable before your different meaning, value, or decision was stated.
rituals.mindBend: Understanding and agreement are separate tasks; combining them makes people defend being understood instead of discussing the actual difference.
rituals.formulaFlow: View They → Name Need → Say Meaning → Receive Own

rituals.name: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
rituals.title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
rituals.goal: Separate the current incident, recurring pattern, and whole relationship history before deciding what each means — convert current charge.
rituals.steps:

3. Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context.

rituals.name: SET THE CONTACT DOSE
rituals.title: SET THE CONTACT DOSE
rituals.goal: Steady quiet pace; choose the smallest contact dose that preserves both connection and steadiness.
rituals.steps:

2. Start with the lowest dose that keeps both connection and steadiness.
3. Review afterward using your body and behaviour, not guilt.

rituals.name: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
rituals.title: MAP THE RELATIONSHIP LABOUR
rituals.goal: See who carries the hidden work of the relationship over a set period; rebuild shared connection.
rituals.steps:
1. Over a set period, note who starts contact, adjusts, repairs, plans, and follows up emotionally.
2. Allow for real differences in time, health, or capacity.
3. Discuss the pattern by category, not accusation, and ask for one clear rebalance.

rituals.win: The hidden jobs became visible enough to support one clear request for a fairer balance.

rituals.name: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
rituals.title: POSTURE WITHOUT PROPHECY
rituals.goal: Use a stable open posture without treating posture as a prediction about the outcome — sort false noise.
rituals.steps:
1. Take a stable, non-defensive position: feet supported, spine available, gaze level, arms unguarded enough for safety.
2. Do not use the posture to predict success or failure.
3. Keep the posture while you wait for actual evidence.
rituals.winReward: Your body stayed supported and non-defensive while actual evidence, not pose, decided what the situation meant.
rituals.win: Your body stayed supported and non-defensive while actual evidence, not pose, decided what the situation meant.
rituals.mindBend: Posture can change available behaviour without being a prophecy. Confidence in the body does not guarantee what happens next.
rituals.formulaFlow: Adopt → Refuse Prophecy → Hold Evidence

rituals.name: SOFT JAW, SAME BOUNDARY
rituals.title: SOFT JAW, SAME BOUNDARY
rituals.goal: Release heavy load; lower jaw tension while keeping the exact boundary unchanged.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice jaw pressure before speaking.
2. Separate the teeth, relax the tongue, and exhale naturally.
3. Deliver the exact limit you planned—no extra smile, apology, or attack.
4. Let articulation stay clear while muscular threat signalling drops.
rituals.winReward: The limit was spoken clearly without added apology, attack, or performative friendliness.
rituals.win: The limit was spoken clearly without added apology, attack, or performative friendliness.

rituals.name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
rituals.title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
rituals.ritual_name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
rituals.goal: Prefer the option whose failure becomes visible while correction is still practical; repair small bridge.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

rituals.name: UNWIND IN REVERSE
rituals.title: UNWIND IN REVERSE
rituals.goal: Exit tight spiral: release a tension chain in the reverse order that it built.
rituals.steps:
1. Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.
rituals.winReward: Each muscle group handed the release onward until you could compare the original bracing point with its starting state.
rituals.win: Each muscle group handed the release onward until you could compare the original bracing point with its starting state.

rituals.name: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
rituals.title: BORROW STILLNESS FROM THE WALL
rituals.goal: Use an imagined stable line as a reference without forcing your inner state to copy it; reconnect useful link.

1. Picture a stable horizontal line or horizon.
2. Notice its imagined stillness beside the movement inside your body and mind.
3. Do not force inner movement to match the line.
4. Let the stable image become a reference for one slow breath.
rituals.winReward: Movement inside could continue while one slow breath borrowed orientation from something pictured as still.
rituals.win: Movement inside could continue while one slow breath borrowed orientation from something pictured as still.
rituals.mindBend: Stability can be used as a reference without becoming a demand. Contrast may organise attention better than forced matching.

rituals.name: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
rituals.title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE
rituals.goal: Patch fresh break: use near, middle, and far sounds to reopen the sense of space around you.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot the nearest sound, one mid-distance sound, and the farthest audible layer.
2. Move attention outward through those distances, then back once.
3. Let the far sound widen the perceived space around the closest one.
rituals.winReward: Attention travelled outward and back once, and the farthest sound made the nearest layer feel less enclosing.
rituals.win: Attention travelled outward and back once, and the farthest sound made the nearest layer feel less enclosing.

rituals.title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
rituals.ritual_name: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
rituals.goal: Keep only the room function that supports the next safe action and dismiss the rest for now; unhook repeating orbit.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture four ordinary things from a familiar room.
2. Give each only its basic job: support, light, hold, open.
3. Say NOT NEEDED NOW to every function irrelevant to this moment.
4. Keep only the imagined function that supports your next safe action.

rituals.name: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
rituals.title: HIDE THE OPTION NAMES
rituals.goal: Compare options on relevant traits before reconnecting them to their emotionally loaded names; stitch broken connection.
rituals.steps:
1. In your mind, rename the leading options A, B, and C.
2. Pick three relevant traits such as time, fit, reliability, or learning.
3. Compare A, B, and C only on those traits without adding new arguments.
4. Reconnect each letter to its option and notice what truly changed the ranking.
rituals.winReward: A, B, and C changed or kept their ranking based on time, fit, reliability, or learning rather than identity.
rituals.win: A, B, and C changed or kept their ranking based on time, fit, reliability, or learning rather than identity.

rituals.name: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
rituals.title: WHEN DOES THIS INFORMATION EXPIRE?
rituals.goal: Repair missing thread; mark old information as expired instead of letting it keep voting in the current decision.
rituals.steps:
1. For each influential input, picture an expiry condition: price changes, role ends, policy updates, health status shifts, deadline passes.
2. Notice any expired item. Stop letting it guide new behaviour until the information is refreshed.
rituals.winReward: At least one influential input received an expiry condition and stopped guiding behaviour once it was stale.
rituals.win: At least one influential input received an expiry condition and stopped guiding behaviour once it was stale.
rituals.mindBend: Old information can keep authority simply because it was once correct. Usefulness needs a current date as much as a fact does.

rituals.title: PARK WHAT YOU CAN’T KNOW YET
rituals.ritual_name: PARK WHAT YOU CAN’T KNOW YET
rituals.goal: Leave familiar spiral: park a problem until the missing information needed to think usefully actually exists.
rituals.steps:
1. Name what is missing: another person’s decision, a test result, a future opening, or a resource.
2. Name what change would make thinking useful again.
3. Until that happens, store the problem with that trigger and stop working it.
rituals.winReward: The missing information got a clear reopening trigger, so the problem no longer needed constant mental work.
rituals.win: The missing information got a clear reopening trigger, so the problem no longer needed constant mental work.
rituals.mindBend: Thinking cannot solve information that does not exist yet. Repeating the calculation only creates more versions of the same gap.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Variable → State Change → Store Away

rituals.title: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
rituals.ritual_name: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
rituals.goal: Identify what kind of effort you are feeling before deciding that effort means failure — restore broken thread.
rituals.steps:
1. Classify the strain using evidence.
2. If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system.
3. Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.
rituals.winReward: Danger, novelty, skill growth, or poor design each received a different response instead of one global verdict.
rituals.win: Danger, novelty, skill growth, or poor design each received a different response instead of one global verdict.
rituals.mindBend: Strain has different causes — treating every difficult feeling as the same message can make learning, danger, and bad design indistinguishable.
rituals.formulaFlow: Use Evidence → Stop Novelty → Respond Category

rituals.name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
rituals.title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
rituals.goal: Exit old orbit: find a work-rest gear that matches actual strain instead of your prediction about strain.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
rituals.winReward: A short work cycle with a deliberate ending revealed whether the next ratio should increase, hold, or finish.
rituals.win: A short work cycle with a deliberate ending revealed whether the next ratio should increase, hold, or finish.
rituals.mindBend: Anticipated effort and experienced effort are different measurements. Testing the gear replaces dread with data.
rituals.formulaFlow: Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: THE BORING DOSE
rituals.title: THE BORING DOSE
rituals.goal: Practise a small, fixed dose of boredom without adding stimulation or extending the challenge — sequence mixed signals.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose a safe boring task and decide on ten slow breaths.
2. Decide that no extra stimulation will be added during those breaths.
3. Notice boredom’s body sensations until the tenth breath.
4. Stop there, even if you could continue; increase future doses slowly.

rituals.name: THREE RINGS OF AGENCY
rituals.title: THREE RINGS OF AGENCY
rituals.goal: Clear rising static; act where you have control, ask where you have influence, and release what you can only watch.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine three rings: CONTROL, INFLUENCE, WATCH.
2. Put each piece of the problem in the right ring in your mind.
3. Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch.

rituals.mindBend: Agency expands when control is made smaller and more accurate. Pretending everything is controllable actually hides the parts that truly are.

rituals.name: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
rituals.title: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
rituals.goal: Delay one answer-seeking urge and watch whether the need for information survives the wait; convert hot pressure.
rituals.steps:
1. When the question demands an answer, picture it and delay asking for a short, chosen interval.
2. Track urge intensity at beginning, middle, and end without researching.
3. Decide afterward whether information is still needed for action or only for relief.
rituals.winReward: The urge was tracked from beginning to end without research, then information was judged by action need rather than relief.
rituals.win: The urge was tracked from beginning to end without research, then information was judged by action need rather than relief.
rituals.mindBend: A question can feel informational when its real job is soothing — delay reveals whether the answer changes action or only reduces discomfort.
rituals.formulaFlow: Question Demands → Track Urge → Decide Afterward

3. Plan from likelihood and safety needs, not possibility alone.

rituals.name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
rituals.title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
rituals.ritual_name: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
rituals.goal: Collapse repeated clues that all came from the same source before judging how much evidence you have; break mental orbit.
rituals.steps:
1. Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.

rituals.name: THREE STORIES CAN’T ALL BE TRUE
rituals.title: THREE STORIES CAN’T ALL BE TRUE
rituals.ritual_name: THREE STORIES CAN’T ALL BE TRUE
rituals.goal: Mend real connection: hold three different explanations open until later evidence shows which one fits best.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep the same unclear cue in mind: a delayed reply, expression, or result.
2. Create three explanations that cannot all be true.
3. Name what later evidence would separate them.
4. Do not commit to one story until support appears.
rituals.winReward: One unclear cue became three possible stories, and certainty waited for evidence.
rituals.win: One unclear cue became three possible stories, and certainty waited for evidence.
rituals.mindBend: Unclear events feel certain when the mind stops making alternatives. Several possible stories expose the gap between a cue and a conclusion.
rituals.formulaFlow: Hold Cue → Make Alternatives → Name Evidence → Wait Evidence

rituals.name: CHOOSE WITH THE UNKNOWN INCLUDED
rituals.title: CHOOSE WITH THE UNKNOWN INCLUDED
rituals.goal: Make the decision once your evidence threshold is met, with the remaining unknowns still named — close tight spiral.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the unknowns, notice which could change the decision, and compare available evidence with your preselected threshold.
2. Once the evidence line is reached, choose while naming what remains uncertain.
3. Build a review point for the critical unknowns.
rituals.winReward: A choice happened without pretending uncertainty had vanished, and critical unknowns received a review point.
rituals.win: A choice happened without pretending uncertainty had vanished, and critical unknowns received a review point.
rituals.mindBend: Good decisions do not require all uncertainty to disappear. They require enough evidence plus a plan for what still matters later.
rituals.formulaFlow: Change → Choose Uncertain → Build Review

rituals.name: THE POINT OF NO MORE INFLUENCE
rituals.title: THE POINT OF NO MORE INFLUENCE
rituals.ritual_name: THE POINT OF NO MORE INFLUENCE
rituals.goal: Drop heavy pressure; find the exact point where further effort can no longer influence the outcome and close there.
rituals.steps:
1. Name what you have already done, what remains unknown, and which outcomes no longer respond to effort.
2. Notice the exact boundary where influence ends.
3. Use one physical closing action and redirect into a present responsibility.
rituals.winReward: Completed effort, remaining unknowns, and non-responsive outcomes separated before attention returned to a present responsibility.

rituals.mindBend: Persistence becomes control-seeking after influence ends; recognising the boundary prevents effort from being spent on a result that cannot hear it.

rituals.title: ONE LOCAL REASON
rituals.goal: Find one reason within the next day that deserves ten minutes of your behaviour; exit tight cycle.
rituals.steps:

2. Name why it matters locally.
3. Give it ten minutes of undivided behaviour.

rituals.name: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
rituals.title: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
rituals.ritual_name: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
rituals.goal: Interrupt mental spiral: carry forward one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value without calling the harmful event good.
rituals.steps:
1. State clearly what was wrong or unwanted.
2. Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial.
3. Let the value belong to you, not to the harm.
rituals.winReward: The event stayed wrong while something useful was reclaimed as yours rather than credited to the harm.
rituals.win: The event stayed wrong while something useful was reclaimed as yours rather than credited to the harm.
rituals.mindBend: Growth after pain does not retroactively justify the pain. What you developed can belong to you without becoming evidence that it 'needed' to happen.
rituals.formulaFlow: State Clearly → Name Boundary → Let Value

rituals.name: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
rituals.title: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
rituals.goal: Use the end-of-life view only to rank what deserves a place today — leave familiar cycle.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine looking back from life’s end—not to frighten yourself, but to rank.
2. Which current demand disappears.
3. Which relationship, integrity choice, health need, or contribution remains.
4. Give the surviving priority one concrete slot today.
rituals.winReward: A demand lost importance while one relationship, integrity, health, or contribution priority gained a concrete time slot.
rituals.win: A demand lost importance while one relationship, integrity, health, or contribution priority gained a concrete time slot.
rituals.mindBend: Distance in time can shrink false urgency — many demands look different when judged by whether they would matter at the far edge of life.
rituals.formulaFlow: Imagine Back → Demand → Remain Relationship → Give Surviving

rituals.name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.title: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.ritual_name: THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
rituals.goal: Review only the turning point slowly enough to keep observation separate from motive; order right sequence.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different.
2. Run those ten seconds once in imagination at half speed. Keep only what you can actually observe: words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’
4. Keep that one fact. End the review before building another explanation.
rituals.winReward: One visible change—pause, volume, face, movement, or reply length—was kept while the review ended before explanation multiplied.

rituals.title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.ritual_name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.goal: Tune shared inputs; turn a repetitive thought loop into simple images and interrupt the first repeated meaning.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

rituals.title: CATCH THE MOMENT ‘MINE’ ARRIVES
rituals.goal: Catch the extra moment when a thought or sensation changes from 'there' to 'mine' — untangle warped distortion.
rituals.steps:

3. Do not try to change either moment.

rituals.title: SOFTEN BOTH SIDES OF SEEING

3. Refuse to place all reality on either side.
4. Let seeing or hearing itself become primary for several seconds.

rituals.title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
rituals.goal: Use real task feedback while letting self-commentary remain faint and unanswered at the edge; leave tight spiral.

2. Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.

4. Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

rituals.name: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
rituals.title: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
rituals.goal: Break old cycle: try three ways of paying attention before choosing the one that fits the task.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the same moment three ways: mainly your body, mainly the environment, then both together.
2. Notice what each view shows clearly and what it misses.
3. Use the view that fits the next task best.

rituals.title: THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME

rituals.steps:

3. Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.

3. Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.
4. Repeat with a sound.

display.mindBend: Concepts arrive so quickly that they feel simultaneous with perception. Noticing the order exposes a layer the mind usually compresses.
display.formulaFlow: Look Touch → Catch Bare → Don't Freeze → Repeat Unnamed

rituals.title: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
rituals.ritual_name: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING

rituals.name: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
rituals.title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
rituals.goal: Remove one emotion temporarily to learn what it was contributing, then restore the whole stack; filter mixed noise.
rituals.steps:
1. Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.
rituals.winReward: One feeling was bracketed without deletion, revealing a change in body, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all.
rituals.win: One feeling was bracketed without deletion, revealing a change in body, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all.
rituals.mindBend: Blended emotion can hide division of labour. Temporarily lifting one block shows what job that feeling was doing in the stack.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
rituals.title: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
rituals.goal: Aim sharp impulse: notice the feeling of being ‘the watcher’ without having to keep that position in place.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the subtle feeling that says ‘I am the observer’.
2. Treat that feeling or location as another experience you can notice.
3. Let awareness continue without holding a separate watcher in place.
4. Return to an ordinary action straight afterward.
rituals.winReward: The effort of being the observer was noticed, then ordinary awareness continued without holding that position.
rituals.win: The effort of being the observer was noticed, then ordinary awareness continued without holding that position.
rituals.mindBend: Trying to be the observer can become another identity. Awareness does not need a separate manager standing outside experience.
rituals.formulaFlow: Notice Watcher → Notice Position → Release Watcher → Return Action

rituals.steps:

2. Place those positions as they feel now.
3. Move only one position or distance toward a more workable configuration.
4. Name the real-life action that matches that imagined shift.

rituals.win: A person, obstacle, resource, or goal changed position and produced one concrete move in the actual situation.

rituals.title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE

1. Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action.
2. Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared.
3. Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and do it now.

rituals.name: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
rituals.title: INTERVIEW THE OBSTACLE
rituals.goal: Calibrate shared choices: ask the obstacle what it is protecting and negotiate one step that respects the valid need.
rituals.steps:
1. Give the obstacle a character and ask three questions: What are you protecting.

rituals.title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
rituals.goal: Tune interference; compare three possible endings at the decision point, then choose the one best supported by evidence and values.

rituals.title: WHAT WOULD THIS FACT CHANGE?
rituals.goal: Order shared sequence; collect only facts that could actually change what you decide.
rituals.steps:

2. If no result changes action, stop collecting it.
3. Prioritise the fact with the largest possible decision swing.

rituals.name: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
rituals.title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
rituals.goal: Compare two options at a time using one declared criterion and let the survivor earn the next look; resync signals.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival.
2. Choose one criterion that matters for this round and picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion.
4. Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict.
rituals.winReward: The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.
rituals.win: The bracket produced a next option to inspect without pretending the winner was a permanent life verdict.
rituals.mindBend: Choice overload shrinks when comparisons are local; deciding between two things is cognitively different from holding the whole field at once.
rituals.formulaFlow: Seed Options → Pick Criterion → Play Pairs → Crown Next
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.name: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
rituals.title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
rituals.goal: Disrupt mental orbit; move one inherited rule across different settings and keep only what remains ethical and workable.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.

rituals.win: The rule changed meaning across family, work, and friendship, revealing which parts were universal and which depended on context.

rituals.name: ONE ACTIVE THREAD
rituals.title: ONE ACTIVE THREAD
rituals.goal: Contain extra charge; keep one work thread active and save its resume point before another switch can take over.
rituals.steps:
1. Mentally name the exact restart instruction.
2. Let the urge to keep switching weaken slightly.
3. Mute one distraction that competes with the work lane.
4. Say one usable first line aloud.
5. Settle on the resume point you will return to.
rituals.winReward: One distraction was muted, a usable opening line appeared, and the active thread ended with a clear return marker.
rituals.win: One distraction was muted, a usable opening line appeared, and the active thread ended with a clear return marker.
rituals.mindBend: Working memory is easier to protect by reducing simultaneous threads than by trying to hold every thread more tightly.
rituals.formulaFlow: Store Handoff → Stop Clean → Block Noise → Open It → Set Bookmark

rituals.name: END, THEN MOVE
rituals.title: END, THEN MOVE
rituals.goal: Align shared parts; choose the exact stopping point, perform one closing action, and physically leave.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the exact point where the task is allowed to stop.
2. Notice what your mind predicts will happen if you leave it unfinished.
3. Choose one visible closing action.
4. Do the closing action and step away.
5. Leave the remaining work for the next planned return point.
rituals.winReward: The task stopped at the planned edge, with remaining work assigned to the next return.
rituals.win: The task stopped at the planned edge, with remaining work assigned to the next return.
rituals.mindBend: Stopping feels dangerous when the mind equates unfinished with lost. A visible closure action proves the work can remain incomplete without remaining active.
